reason: H0 only feeds arbitrary bytes to simdjson::dom::parser::parse and never constructs, mutates, or converts a builder::string_builder. S1 changes string_builder::operator std::string() to construct its result from operator std::string_view(), so the builder conversion path and its length/content semantics remain completely unreachable from H0. This is materially distinct from parsing and is fuzz-worthy for arbitrary serialized bytes, embedded NULs, escaping, and boundary lengths.
evidence: H0's sole production operation is parser.parse(Data, Size).get(elem).
The changed source is include/simdjson/generic/ondemand/json_string_builder-inl.h, while H0 exercises simdjson::dom::parser.
S1 changes string_builder::operator std::string() from return std::string(std::string_view()); to return std::string(operator std::string_view());.
The same source exposes input-bearing builder operations such as escape_and_append_with_quotes, append_raw, append, and append_key_value, none of which H0 invokes.
recommended_action: Add a dedicated builder fuzz target that derives operation sequences and payloads from Data, exercises append_raw, escape_and_append_with_quotes, append, and structural methods, then invokes both operator std::string_view() and operator std::string(); assert identical byte content and length, validate produced JSON where appropriate, and include embedded NUL, control-byte, quote, backslash, UTF-8, empty, and capacity-boundary inputs.
